rules.body: Apply this guidance when deferred document edits use a persistent owner distinct from the current observer. README.md states: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge." docs/host-api.md states: "Document buffers are owned by the store BufferBank, while Badge owns only a live subscription." Preserve that ownership separation when introducing coalescing.

Route edits through the existing per-document trailing buffer. Restart the quiet interval on each edit, retain only the latest pending text, and keep the utility reusable after execution. TASK states: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." src/Workflow.java supplies the document binding: "static final class BufferBank {final Map<String,Trailing> entries=new HashMap<>();Trailing get(Environment env,String id){return entries.computeIfAbsent(id,k->new Trailing(env,120,text->env.write(k,text)));}}"

On departure, detach the departing Badge subscription while preserving its store-owned buffer, and flush pending document text before departure returns. Do not cancel away persistent document edits merely because their view detaches. This follows the persistence ownership in README.md and TASK's instruction: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces." Capture the departing Badge and clear current before invoking its save so synchronous navigation cannot cause cleanup to target a newly established view.

Treat flushing as a synchronous reentry boundary. docs/host-api.md states: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." After departure flushes, an outer open must check whether its navigation generation remains current before installing its requested Badge. Preserve the existing request guard in src/Workflow.java: "if(true&&request!=generation)return;" A nested open or close must remain authoritative.

Clear the pending task state before invoking save callbacks, preserving reuse and reentrant edits. src/Workflow.java provides: "void flush() { if(handle!=null)env.cancel(handle); String text=pending; handle=null;pending=null; if(text!=null)work.accept(text); }" Keep the null check rather than treating empty text as absent.

Preserve public methods, document identities, text, status payloads, and subscription behavior. docs/host-api.md states: "createWorkspace offers open(id), edit(text), close(), dispose(); createSearchPreview offers query(text), hide()." It also states: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics."

Do not transfer document persistence policy to preview work. TASK states: "The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." Preserve the preview's 40 ms trailing interval and hide cancellation in src/Workflow.java: "void query(String text){task.push(text);}void hide(){task.cancel();}"

Verify source-derived checkpoints: no individual writes before 120 ms of quiet; one latest-text save after quiet; successful later bursts; empty-text persistence; pending text saved by open, close, and dispose; synchronous save callbacks that open or close remain authoritative; detached Badges stop receiving status events; preview retains its 40 ms interval, discard-on-hide behavior, and later reuse. These checks exercise TASK's coalescing and preservation requirements together with the documented ownership and synchronous listener behavior.

limitations: Applies when document buffers outlive view subscriptions and pending document edits must persist on departure; transient work with discard-on-hide behavior requires a different boundary policy.
Public sources do not define exception guarantees for writes, listeners, scheduling, or output, nor ordering across multiple workspaces sharing a store.
Null document ids and null edit text have no additional specified semantics. Empty strings remain valid text.
Attempt 1 provides supporting observations for this implementation only; one passing attempt establishes neither causality nor cross-task benefit.

notes: Not approved; training acceptance or expert summary does not verify cross-task effectiveness
